bills.title: Bills
bills.subtitle: Recurring payments & schedule
bills.variableAmountDesc: The charge changes each cycle (e.g. energy, gas). The amount you set is just an estimate.
bills.variableAmountHint: Estimated amount — adjust it to what you were actually charged.
bills.variablePayHint: Enter what you were actually charged — it'll become the new estimate for next time.
bills.paysDownLoanHint: Recording this payment splits it into interest (an expense) and principal, and lowers the loan's balance.
bills.loanNeedsAccount: Pick an account to pay from
bills.splitAutoHint: Leave an amount blank to auto-split the remaining balance equally.
bills.splitHelp: The full bill leaves the account, but only your share counts as an expense. Their share is fronted out of the account and tracked under "Owed to You" until they pay you back.
bills.splitPayNote: The full bill leaves this account; only your share is the expense. {name}'s {amount} is fronted and tracked under "Owed to You" — it returns to the account when you record their payment.
bills.splitPayNoteGroup: The full bill leaves this account; only your share is the expense. The other {n} people's {amount} is fronted and tracked under "Owed to You" — it returns as you record each person's payment.
bills.splitExpenseHelp: Paid for something shared (like dinner)? Log it once and split it across people. Your share counts as an expense; everyone else's share is fronted from the account and tracked under "Owed to You" until they pay you back.
bills.splitModePerPersonHint: Enter each person's amount — the total adds up automatically.
bills.splitSmartHint: Enter a total to divide it among everyone (blank boxes split the rest), or leave the total empty and type each person's amount to add it up.
bills.includeMe: Include my share in the split
bills.splitExpenseNeedPeople: Add at least one person with a share.
bills.splitExpenseOverTotal: Everyone's shares add up to more than the total.

funding.title: Funding
funding.subtitle: Front a shared bill as a Group Tab, or pool real cash in a Group Vault
funding.noAccountsDesc: You need at least one account to charge spends to and receive paybacks into.
funding.emptyDesc: Create a Group Tab to front a shared bill and track who owes you, or a Group Vault to pool real savings for an upcoming goal.
funding.virtualHint: A Group Tab is a virtual budget — you front the money and track who pays you back. Spends charge to a real account; paybacks settle the tab.
funding.myShareHint: Only your share counts as your personal expense. The rest is fronting the group's money.
funding.confirmDeleteSpend: Delete this spend? Its ledger rows will be reversed.
funding.paymentHint: Record money a participant paid you back. It lands in your account but never counts as income.
funding.confirmDeletePayment: Delete this payback? Its ledger row will be reversed.
funding.confirmDelete: Delete this pool? Its cash movements will be reversed.
funding.realHint: A Group Vault holds real cash in an account you choose. Others' contributions land there as money you're holding; your own share is just earmarked. Spends draw directly from the vault.
funding.realMembersHint: Members start at $0 — use Add money on the card to record real contributions.
funding.settledDesc: All participants have paid back their share. Would you like to archive this Group Tab?
funding.deleteDesc: This will reverse {n} transaction(s) across your accounts and cannot be undone.
funding.deleteDescEmpty: This pool has no transactions. Deleting it is safe.
funding.contributionHint: Record real money going into the pool. Your own money moves from one of your accounts; everyone else's is cash you're holding for the group.
funding.confirmDeleteContribution: Remove this contribution? Its ledger row will be reversed.
funding.migrateTitle: Move pool to a real account
funding.migrateDesc: This pool's cash sits in an old holding account. Move it into a real account so its balance reflects the money flow.
funding.migrateHint: Pick the real account that holds this pool's cash. Every contribution and spend will move onto it, and the old holding account will be removed.
funding.editVirtualHint: Add or remove people and adjust pledges — the pool total updates to match. Removing someone who already paid you back will reverse those paybacks.
funding.editRealHint: To add or remove contributors or change the amount, use Add money or edit the contributions below — real cash always moves through those.
funding.confirmDropPaid: Removing these people will reverse {n} payback(s) they made. Continue?

credit.title: Smart Credit Report
credit.subtitle: Track utilization and grow your credit score
credit.emptyDesc: Add a credit card on the Accounts page to start tracking your credit utilization and score tips.
credit.overallSub: Across all cards with a limit set
credit.noLimitsDesc: Add each card's limit below to see your utilization and tips.
credit.setLimitPrompt: Add this card's credit limit to track utilization.
credit.cashBackHint: Applies as a statement credit — lowers your balance and is not counted as income.
credit.payBeforeStmt: {card} statement closes in {days}d — pay {amount} to report under {pct}%
credit.statementDayHint: Day of the month your statement closes (1–31). Powers pay-before-statement reminders.
credit.alertOverDesc: High utilization is the fastest factor to drag down a score. Paying these below {pct}% — ideally before the statement closes — is the quickest win.
credit.allGoodDesc: Every card is under the recommended {pct}%. Keep it up!
credit.tipsTitle: How to grow your credit score
credit.tip1Body: Keep each card and your overall balance under 30% of the limit — under 10% is best. Amounts owed make up about 30% of a FICO score.
credit.tip2Body: Issuers usually report your statement balance, not what's left after the due date. Paying down before the statement date lowers the utilization that gets reported.
credit.tip3Body: Payment history is the single biggest factor (about 35%). Set autopay for at least the minimum so you're never late.
credit.tip4Body: Length of history and your total available limit both help. Closing a card shortens your history and shrinks your limit, which raises utilization.
credit.tip5Body: A higher limit lowers utilization without paying anything down. Ask after 6–12 months of on-time payments — just avoid a hard pull if you can.
credit.tip6Body: If one card is maxed, moving part of the balance to another card lowers your highest single-card utilization, which lenders also watch.
credit.simSub: NovaFi estimates what you can pay from your income, bills, budgets, loans and splits — then splits it to clear the most over-{pct}% cards first.
credit.simPrompt: Enter an amount above to see your optimal split.
credit.simNoFreeCash: Your bills, budgets and loans use up this month's predicted income, so there's nothing left to suggest. Enter an amount above to plan anyway.
credit.simNotEnoughData: Income estimates improve with more history — you have {months} month(s) of data so far. Add at least 3 months for the best results. You can still enter an amount manually below.
credit.simIncomeAverage: Based on your average income (last 3 months)
credit.simIncomeCurrent: Based on this month's income so far
credit.simTowardIdeal: Already under {pct}% — this pushes you toward the 10% ideal.
credit.simNothing: This won't clear a full spike yet, but every dollar still lowers utilization.
credit.advSub: These cards run high but you've paid them down consistently — asking for a higher limit dilutes utilization with zero cash out.
credit.arbSub: Bureaus report your balance on the closing date, not the due date — pay these down first to lower reported utilization.
credit.arbItem: {card} closes in {days} day(s): pay {amount} to report under {pct}%
credit.arbItemToday: {card} closes today: pay {amount} to report under {pct}%
credit.bxSub: High-interest balances quietly cost you — moving them to a 0% card keeps that interest in your pocket.
credit.bxMove: Move {amount} to {dest} to save about {savings} over {months} months
credit.bxMoveHypo: A 0% balance-transfer card could save about {savings} over {months} months

settings.title: Settings
settings.subtitle: Taxes, payroll & preferences
settings.displayNameDesc: Shown in your dashboard greeting. Leave blank to use your Google account name.
settings.appUpdateDesc: If the app feels stale after an update — especially when launched from your home screen — use this to clear all caches and reload the latest version. Your data in Google Sheets is never affected.
settings.budgetRolloverDesc: Carry unused budget (surplus or deficit) forward to the next month. Underspending adds to next month's limit; overspending reduces it.
settings.darkModeDesc: Switch to a darker color scheme, easier on the eyes at night.
settings.signOutDesc: Sign out of NovaFi on this device. You'll be asked to confirm first.
settings.deleteAllDataDesc: Permanently erase all your financial data — accounts, transactions, bills, budgets, goals, and everything else. This cannot be undone.
settings.deleteAllStep1Title: Are you sure you want to delete all data?
settings.deleteAllStep1Body: This will permanently erase every account, transaction, bill, budget, goal, paycheck, loan, and setting stored in your Google Sheet. There is no undo.
settings.deleteAllStep2Placeholder: I want to delete my data
settings.deleteAllStep2Hint: Type exactly: I want to delete my data
settings.deleteAllSuccess: All data deleted. Signing you out.
settings.deleteAllFailed: Failed to delete data. Please try again.
settings.contactsDesc: Manage the people you split bills and expenses with. They appear in every split picker across the app.
settings.contactsEmpty: No contacts yet. Add someone to split bills and expenses with.
settings.contactsNote: Contacts are saved to your Google Sheet, so they're available on every device. Removing one keeps any past shared-payment records intact.
